DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Meena Krishnan
Diagnosis: Osteoarthritis of the right knee.
Procedure: Right total knee replacement.
Medications: Take Paracetamol 500 mg twice daily after meals for 5 days. Take Omeprazole 20 mg once daily before breakfast for 5 days.
Lab Diagnostics: Right Knee X-Ray (AP & Lateral) & CRP test scheduled on October 12, 2026.
Activity: Walk with the assistance of a walker. Perform the prescribed knee exercises twice daily.
Wound Care: Keep the surgical wound clean and dry. Do not soak the wound.
Diet: Continue a normal balanced vegetarian diet and drink adequate fluids.
Follow-up: Visit the orthopedic clinic after 1 week.
Warning signs: Contact the hospital immediately if you develop fever, severe swelling, increasing pain, or unusual discharge from the wound.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Ravi Kumar
Diagnosis: Recovery after cardiac bypass surgery.
Medications: Take Aspirin 75 mg once daily after breakfast. Take Atorvastatin 40 mg once daily at bedtime.
Lab Diagnostics: Fasting Lipid Profile, ECG and Serum Electrolytes scheduled on October 6, 2026.
Activity: Avoid heavy lifting. Walk for 10 minutes twice daily and increase gradually as tolerated.
Diet: Follow a low-sodium diet and avoid adding extra salt.
Follow-up: Cardiology review after 7 days.
Warning signs: Seek urgent medical attention for severe chest pain, severe breathlessness, or fainting.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Lakshmi Devi
Diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia.
Medications: Take Amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily after meals for 7 days. Take the prescribed fever medicine as needed.
Lab Diagnostics: Repeat Chest X-Ray and Complete Blood Count (CBC) scheduled on October 10, 2026.
Activity: Rest adequately and walk gently as tolerated.
Hydration: Drink adequate fluids throughout the day.
Follow-up: Review with the physician after 3 days.
Warning signs: Contact the hospital for worsening breathlessness, persistent high fever, confusion, or blue lips.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Arjun Menon
Diagnosis: Left ankle fracture after fixation.
Medications: Take Paracetamol 500 mg as directed for pain.
Lab Diagnostics: Left ankle weight-bearing X-ray series scheduled on October 4, 2026.
Activity: Use crutches and do not put full weight on the injured ankle until reviewed.
Exercise: Perform the ankle and toe exercises twice daily as demonstrated by physiotherapy.
Follow-up: Orthopedic review after 2 weeks.
Warning signs: Seek help for severe swelling, numbness, blue discoloration, or uncontrolled pain.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Sita Rao
Diagnosis: Diabetes follow-up.
Medications: Take Metformin 500 mg twice daily with meals.
Lab Diagnostics: HbA1c and Fasting Blood Glucose (FBG) evaluation scheduled on October 13, 2026.
Diet: Follow the diabetic meal plan and avoid skipping meals.
Monitoring: Check blood glucose according to the clinic plan and record the readings.
Follow-up: Diabetes clinic after 1 week.
Warning signs: Seek medical help for severe weakness, confusion, or loss of consciousness.
Note: The dose is not to be changed without clinician advice.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Vikram Shah
Diagnosis: Recovery after laparoscopic appendectomy.
Medications: Take Paracetamol 500 mg twice daily after food for 3 days.
Lab Diagnostics: Complete Blood Count (CBC) and Liver Function Test (LFT) scheduled on October 11, 2026.
Wound Care: Keep the incision clean and dry. Do not soak the wound.
Activity: Avoid strenuous exercise for 2 weeks.
Follow-up: Surgical review after 1 week.
Warning signs: Contact the hospital for fever, increasing abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, or wound discharge.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Anitha Joseph
Diagnosis: Recovery after laparoscopic gallbladder surgery.
Medications: Take the prescribed pain medicine after meals as directed.
Lab Diagnostics: Post-arthroplasty pelvic & hip radiography series scheduled on October 15, 2026.
Diet: Follow a low-fat diet for the first week and eat smaller meals.
Activity: Walk gently every day and avoid strenuous activity for 2 weeks.
Follow-up: Surgical clinic after 1 week.
Warning signs: Contact the hospital for fever, worsening abdominal pain, yellowing of the eyes, or persistent vomiting.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Karthik Srinivasan
Diagnosis: Recovery after ACL reconstruction.
Medications: Take Paracetamol 500 mg twice daily after meals for 5 days.
Lab Diagnostics: Abdominal ultrasound and Hemoglobin evaluation scheduled on October 12, 2026.
Activity: Use the knee brace and crutches as instructed. Do not drive until cleared.
Exercise: Complete the prescribed physiotherapy exercises twice daily.
Follow-up: Orthopedic review after 1 week.
Warning signs: Seek help for severe calf swelling, sudden shortness of breath, or increasing knee pain.
